name: groundnut
sowing_season: Kharif: June–July with the monsoon | Summer: January–February (irrigated)
soil: Light, well-drained sandy loam with enough calcium, pH 6.0–7.5; loose soil lets the pegs go in easily

stages.name: Germination / Emergence
stages.irrigation: Sow in moist soil. Summer crop: irrigate before sowing, then lightly if the soil dries.
stages.fertilizer: Basal: 45 kg DAP + 15–20 kg MOP per acre. Treat seed with Trichoderma 4 g per kg (or Thiram 3 g per kg), then Rhizobium 5 g per kg.
watch_for: Collar rot — seedlings rot at the base
Birds and squirrels digging out seed
tips: Shell pods just before sowing; 40–50 kg kernels per acre for bunch types
Rows 30 cm apart, plants 10 cm apart

stages.name: Vegetative Growth
stages.irrigation: Kharif: drain extra rain. Summer: every 8–10 days. Mild dryness at this stage is fine.
tips: Weed and hoe at 15 and 30 days — no hoeing once pegging starts
A short dry spell now brings more flowers later

stages.name: Flowering / Pegging
stages.description: Flowers appear and the pegs (needles) grow down into the soil to form pods.
stages.irrigation: Critical stage — keep the soil moist (every 7–10 days in summer).
stages.fertilizer: Gypsum 200 kg per acre near the plants at flowering, then light earthing up — it fills the pods and gives better kernels.
watch_for: Tobacco caterpillar eating leaves at night
tips: Do not disturb the soil after the pegs go in
Light earthing up after gypsum helps more pegs reach the soil

stages.name: Pod Formation / Pod Filling
stages.description: Pods develop under the soil and kernels fill.
stages.irrigation: Every 10–12 days; water stress now gives empty pods.
watch_for: Stem rot — white fungal threads at the stem base
tips: For tikka and rust spray Hexaconazole 5 EC 2 ml/litre or Mancozeb 2.5 g/litre
Repeat after 15 days if spots keep spreading

stages.name: Maturity / Harvest
stages.description: Leaves turn yellow and the inside of the shell darkens.
stages.irrigation: Stop 10–15 days before harvest; a light irrigation before lifting helps if the soil is hard.
watch_for: Aflatoxin mould if pods stay wet
tips: Pull a few plants: harvest when 70–80% of pods have a dark inner shell
Dry pods to 8–9% moisture before storage

common_pests.name: Tobacco caterpillar
common_pests.symptoms: Leaves eaten in groups at night, only veins left
common_pests.control: Emamectin benzoate 5 SG 0.4 g/litre; collect egg masses; pheromone traps 5 per acre

common_pests.name: Leaf miner
common_pests.symptoms: Brown blotches on leaves, folded leaves with small caterpillars
common_pests.control: Neem seed kernel extract (5%); light traps

common_pests.name: White grub
common_pests.symptoms: Plants wilt and dry in patches; C-shaped grubs in the soil
common_pests.control: Deep summer ploughing; collect and destroy beetles from nearby trees after the first rains

common_diseases.name: Tikka leaf spot
common_diseases.symptoms: Brown (early) or black (late) round spots on leaves, early leaf fall
common_diseases.control: Hexaconazole 5 EC 2 ml/litre or Mancozeb 2.5 g/litre, 2–3 sprays 15 days apart

common_diseases.name: Collar rot
common_diseases.symptoms: Seedlings rot at soil level with black fungal growth
common_diseases.control: Seed treatment with Trichoderma 4 g or Thiram 3 g per kg

common_diseases.name: Stem rot
common_diseases.symptoms: White threads and mustard-like seeds at the stem base; the plant wilts
common_diseases.control: Trichoderma mixed with FYM in the soil; gypsum; deep ploughing
